purpose: Quetiapine is used to treat conditions like schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depression. It helps reduce symptoms like hallucinations, mood swings, and feelings of sadness or hopelessness. Sometimes it is also used at low doses to help with sleep, though this is considered an off-label use.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called dopamine and serotonin to communicate. In conditions like schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, these chemicals can become unbalanced. Quetiapine works by blocking certain receptors for these chemicals, helping to bring them back into a healthier balance so you feel more stable and think more clearly.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include feeling drowsy or sleepy, dry mouth, dizziness especially when standing up quickly, weight gain, constipation, and blurred vision. Many of these tend to be worse when you first start the medication and may improve over time.
warnings: Quetiapine can increase blood sugar levels, so it is important to monitor for signs of diabetes like increased thirst or frequent urination. It may raise the risk of falls due to dizziness, especially in older adults. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms. This medication also carries a warning about an increased risk of suicidal thoughts in young adults, especially in the first few weeks, so contact your doctor right away if your mood worsens.
typical_dosing: Dosing varies widely depending on what condition is being treated. For schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, doses typically range from 150 mg to 800 mg per day, usually split into two doses. For depression, lower doses around 50 mg to 300 mg per day are common. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, and never change your dose on your own.
